title: 02 — Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
html:
02 — Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation

The one idea: estimation exists to pick the architecture, not to be precise. Round everything to a power of ten, write assumptions down, and let the order of magnitude tell you whether you need one database or a hundred.

1. Numbers to have in your head

1.1 Powers of two

Power Exact Approx Name
2^10 1,024 1 thousand 1 KB
2^20 1,048,576 1 million 1 MB
2^30 1 billion 1 GB
2^40 1 trillion 1 TB
2^50 1 quadrillion 1 PB

1.2 Latency — the ratios matter more than the values

Operation Rough time Relative
L1 cache reference ~1 ns 1
Main memory reference ~100 ns 100×
Compress 1 KB (fast codec) ~2 µs
Read 1 MB sequentially from memory ~10 µs
Round trip within a data centre ~0.5 ms 500,000×
Read 1 MB sequentially from SSD ~1 ms
Disk seek (HDD) ~10 ms
Round trip across a continent ~50–80 ms
Round trip across the world ~150 ms

What to take from it: memory is fast, disk seeks are slow, network round trips dominate distributed designs. Compress before sending; batch to avoid round trips; keep hot data in memory.

1.3 Availability — "the nines"

SLA Downtime / year Downtime / month
99% 3.65 days 7.3 h
99.9% 8.8 h 43.8 min
99.95% 4.4 h 21.9 min
99.99% 52.6 min 4.4 min
99.999% 5.3 min 26 s

Serial dependencies multiply: three 99.9% services in a chain ≈ 99.7%.

1.4 Time shortcuts

  • 1 day ≈ 86,400 s ≈ 10^5 s (use 100k)
  • 1 month ≈ 2.5 × 10^6 s
  • 1 year ≈ 3 × 10^7 s

2. The method

---
title: Estimation method — DAU to QPS, storage and bandwidth
---
flowchart LR
    A["Users<br/>DAU"] --> B["Actions / user / day"]
    B --> C["Average QPS<br/>= DAU × actions ÷ 10^5"]
    C --> D["Peak QPS<br/>≈ 2–5 × average"]
    B --> E["Bytes / action"]
    E --> F["Storage / day<br/>× retention"]
    E --> G["Bandwidth<br/>= QPS × bytes"]
  1. Write the assumptions as a list others can challenge and correct.
  2. Compute QPS (average, then peak), separately for reads and writes.
  3. Compute storage per day, then over the retention period, then × replication factor.
  4. Compute bandwidth in and out.
  5. Say what the number means: "12k write QPS is beyond one SQL primary comfortably, so we'll shard or use a store built for write throughput."

3. Worked example: a Twitter-like service

Assumptions

  • 300M MAU, 50% daily → 150M DAU
  • Each user posts 2 tweets/day
  • 10% of tweets carry media; media averages 1 MB; text + metadata ≈ 300 B
  • Keep data 5 years

Write QPS

  • 150M × 2 = 300M tweets/day
  • 300M ÷ 10^5 ≈ 3,000 tweets/s average, ~6–10k/s peak

Storage

  • Text: 300M × 300 B = 90 GB/day
  • Media: 300M × 10% × 1 MB = 30 TB/day
  • 5 years: 30 TB × 365 × 5 ≈ 55 PB (media dominates — it goes in object storage, not the DB)

Reads — if the timeline is read 100× per tweet written: ~300k reads/s → caching and fan-out are mandatory (→ chapter 11).

4. Tips that save you in the room

  • Round hard. 86,400 → 100,000. 1,024 → 1,000. Nobody is grading arithmetic.
  • Label units at every line. KB vs Kb vs KiB mistakes are the usual error.
  • Separate read and write paths; they usually differ by 10–1000× and lead to different designs.
  • Peak, not average, sizes the system; average sizes the bill.
  • Replication factor (usually 3) multiplies storage.
  • Stop when the answer changes the design. If it doesn't, you've estimated enough.

5. .NET / Azure mapping

Estimate What it tells you in Azure terms
< ~1k write QPS, < 1 TB A single Azure SQL database (General Purpose / Business Critical) is fine
1k–20k write QPS Azure SQL Hyperscale, or partitioned Cosmos DB
> 20k write QPS or multi-TB/day Cosmos DB / Cassandra-style store, Event Hubs for ingestion
Large binary data Blob Storage (hot/cool/archive tiers), never the database
Cosmos DB sizing Estimate RU/s: a 1 KB point read ≈ 1 RU, a 1 KB write ≈ 5–6 RU

6. Review checklist

  • Assumptions written down before arithmetic.
  • DAU → QPS (avg and peak), reads and writes separately.
  • Storage over retention, including replication.
  • Bandwidth if media is involved.
  • One sentence per number on what it means for the design.
